highlights.title: Anthropic’s AI gave Philadelphia police a fake tip about an unsolved homicide
highlights.summary: An Anthropic AI model provided false information about an unsolved homicide to a Philadelphia Police Department (PPD) tipline, according to a report from 6abc. In a statement released on Friday, the PPD said the AI model sent the tip through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com on July 18th, but the…
body: The false tip ‘purported to come from someone who might have information about the case.’

Anthropic learned its AI model sent the false tip on September 28th and notified the PPD on October 7th. The company said that during testing, its AI model was interacting with “randomly selected websites” and submitted false information through the PPD’s tipline, according to the PPD’s statement. The submission “purported to come from someone who might have information about the case,” the PPD said.

After discovering the submission, Anthropic halted the testing process that led to the false tip. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google have been the subject of increased scrutiny after disclosing that their AI models escaped testing environments and hacked third-party companies. Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic, advocated for slowing down the development of AI in response to these incidents.
Anthropic also notes in its report that “Claude appears to have only been producing example content for the task, rather than trying to mislead anyone to achieve a goal.”

highlights.summary: Former world champion Michael Smith says he plans on "playing 100 per cent of the tournaments" in 2027 after an opening win at the Swiss Darts Trophy.
body: 'Bully Boy' Smith fought back from 3-1 down to beat Rob Owen, hitting 50 per cent of his doubles in just his fourth European Tour event of the season.
"I've missed this. I want to apologise and also make a promise in 2027 I will be playing 100 per cent of the tournaments. You will see me back," said the 2023 world champion.
Smith is chasing down the final spots in the European Championship race and the St Helens thrower beat Owen 6-4 to set up a meeting with Jermaine Wattimena for a place in Sunday's action.

Rob Cross was Friday's standout performer for the second event in a row, averaging 105.95 in his 6-3 success against Mario Vandenbogaerde and will take on Luke Woodhouse on the back of his brilliant opening round performance at the World Grand Prix.

highlights.summary: Alejandro Hidalgo, director of “The Exorcism of God,” is set to make “The Hungry One,” a supernatural horror film unfolding over Malaysia’s Hungry Ghost Festival. Kuala Lumpur-based Abnormal Studios is handling worldwide sales and is introducing the project at the Busan International Film…
body: Filmmaker and entrepreneur Justin Leong is driving the project through Los Angeles-based Lightning Pictures.

“Growing up in Asia, I always felt the Hungry Ghost Festival was incredibly rich visually, from the fire and offerings to the rituals and mythology behind it. When you capture that and shoot it cinematically, it’s movie gold. It gives us a world that audiences may not have seen before, but one that feels immediately atmospheric, mysterious and made for horror,” Leong said.
Leong, who has deep ties to Malaysian-Chinese culture, drew on his own family’s traditions to shape the story.

Hidalgo’s first feature, “The House at the End of Time,” remains Venezuela’s biggest horror hit at the box office. It earned strong notices on the festival circuit and has since gathered a cult audience for mixing the supernatural with science fiction. His 2021 follow-up, “The Exorcism of God,” bowed at Fantastic Fest and went on to sell to more than 150 countries, with Saban Films handling its U.S. theatrical release. It ended 2022 as the highest-grossing Latin American film worldwide.

highlights.title: ‘Pure insanity’: Mathematicians will need years to make sense of OpenAI’s latest drop
highlights.summary: "Staggering." "Overwhelming." "Unprecedented." "Surreal." "Pure insanity." Those were among the descriptions more than three dozen mathematicians reached for in conversations with The Verge as they tried to make sense of the flood of mathematical results OpenAI abruptly dropped on the field this…
body: Careers upended overnight, academics will have to separate solutions from slop while OpenAI moves on.

In all, OpenAI released nearly 400 AI-generated results. These were spread across more than 700 manuscripts and covered a diverse array of mathematical disciplines, including combinatorics, several branches of geometry, number theory, theoretical computer science, algebra, topology, probability and statistical mechanics, and mathematical physics. The collection is so vast that OpenAI felt the need to publish guidance on how to navigate the sprawling GitHub repository.

The sheer volume of work makes even a preliminary assessment as to exactly what the company has released difficult. In the hours and days following the drop, most mathematicians The Verge spoke with said they were still struggling to digest everything; several said that simply working through the roughly 40-page table of contents and abstracts took them the better part of an hour. “Just going over the entire list of abstracts is overwhelming,” said Álvaro Lozano-Robledo, a professor of mathematics at the University of Connecticut.

highlights.title: Pokémon Winds and Waves' Water Starter Breaks a Series Curse
highlights.summary: Every starter in a new Pokémon generation erects an army of staunch defenders, but like it or not, some monsters are loved more than others. And for a couple of decades now, it seems like fire-type starters and grass-type starters keep taking turns stealing the spotlight.
body: Fans seemed receptive to Pokémon Scarlet and Violet 's Quaxly, but the blue duck was ultimately overshadowed by the cult of Sprigatito. I barely saw any hype for Sobble in the generation preceding Scarlet and Violet. The adorable Popplio did inspire a defense squad, but that support was a response to the widespread hatred the poor circus sea lion suffered when it was initially revealed. Oshawott was adorable, but Snivvy's smile stole more hearts back then. Piplup had some champions, but its fandom was pitiful compared to the church of Mudkip that preceded it.

This is the curse of the water starter, who has had the bad luck of sporting some of the weakest designs out of any given trio for at least a few generations of games now. Gequa, the water gecko introduced for Pokémon Winds and Waves, might be the first real contender to the throne. Already, fans keep joking that it is the better version of Sobble, the slack-jawed water starter from the previous generation.

So, Douglas took matters into his own hands. “One time I said, ‘Dad, you remember one Christmas you bought me two beautiful Italian soft leather suitcases? highlights.title: Neanderthal wooden tools from Spain found preserved in stone
highlights.summary: The Stone Age owes its name to tools that survived to our time. The material early humans worked with most, though, was probably wood because it is so much easier to process. Unfortunately, we know very little about Paleolithic woodwork because wood rots relatively quickly.
body: In a recent Science Advances study, a team of Spanish archaeologists has cataloged 597 wooden remains from Neanderthal living areas dating from 62,000 to 40,000 years ago. They found spears, digging sticks, bark trays, parts of shelters, and a club unlike anything seen before, suggesting Neanderthals were likely much more than just Homo sapiens’ dumber cousins.

The oldest wooden artifacts we have are mostly weapons. They include spears from a German town called Schöningen, a spear tip from Clacton-on-Sea in England, and the spear found alongside an elephant skeleton in Lehringen, Germany. Most came from waterlogged sediments, where a lack of oxygen slowed decay.

The spears mostly give us information about how Neanderthals hunted. The findings at Abric Romaní are different because the finds come from a place where Neanderthals lived, slept, cooked, and made tools over the course of some 20,000 years.
points: The Stone Age owes its name to tools that survived to our time.
The material early humans worked with most, though, was probably wood because it is so much easier to process.
Unfortunately, we know very little about Paleolithic woodwork because wood rots relatively quickly.

highlights.title: Magic: The Gathering Returns to Marvel with Darkhold Destiny
highlights.summary: Magic: The Gathering and Marvel have already crossed over a couple of times with Spider-Man and the Marvel Super Heroes set last year. But for its third Marvel set, MTG is getting spooky with Darkhold Destiny.
body: Rather than being based in a fairly mundane version of New York, Darkhold Destiny is taking the likes of Doctor Strange and the Asgardians and telling a more magical story (forgive me). What really separates this new out-there set from the other two Marvel sets is that Wizards of the Coast was really able to write its own story with Marvel's characters and settings, which makes them feel less like a crossover and more like a part of Magic's multiverse.

With a new story written in-house, Wizards of the Coast was also able to give its artists more license to create their own takes on Marvel characters. For instance, with Scarlet Witch in the Marvel Super Heroes set, she looks like a pretty standard take on her comic book appearance. But in the art I was shown for Darkhold Destiny, she looks much more like an MTG character, while still retaining some of the signature parts of her outfit – the mask is still there.

highlights.title: Ukraine’s drones knock out AI data center belonging to "Russia’s Google"
highlights.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes have knocked out two of five data centers belonging to the Russian tech giant Yandex. The damage has left Yandex, known as “Russia’s Google” because it operates the country’s most popular search engine, struggling to maintain its AI chatbot and other online services.
body: The Ukrainian drones struck Yandex data centers in the Sasovo and Kaluga regions of Russia on October 8 and October 9, according to Reuters. Those actions came as a direct response to a Russian drone strike campaign targeting Ukraine’s data centers, which has disrupted mobile phone and Internet services for thousands of Ukrainians since late September.

“We continue to respond to Russia’s attacks on Ukraine, and we’re doing so with high precision,” said Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in a post on X. “Another data center was hit as well—our symmetrical response.”

The Ukrainian company Firepoint said its FP-1 one-way attack drones were involved in the latest strike on the Kaluga data center that is Yandex’s largest such facility, Reuters reported. The first Ukrainian attack targeted Yandex’s Sasovo data center that houses two of the company’s three supercomputers used for training the company’s YandexGPT AI model.

body: Nikon says it’s revisiting its competition rules after the original winner’s video was too good to be true.

In a comment on LinkedIn, Dr. Xu admitted to using AI for the video: “An unsupervised neural-network method was subsequently used for AI-assisted post-processing to distinguish and visualize features in the reconstructed grayscale images from the super-resolution optical imaging.”

Dr. Xu’s video has now been disqualified and appears to have been removed from Nikon’s website. A video from Nguyen Nam Nhat now holds first place, according to the contest’s updated rankings. Following the incident, Nikon says it plans to “revisit rules and evaluation procedures for future competition entries.” It also noted in its statement on the contest that the decision to disqualify Dr. Xu’s video “should not be interpreted as a judgment of the entrant’s professional reputation, scientific contributions, or intent.”

body: Angel Reese scored 22 points and Rhyne Howard added 21 as Atlanta survived a second-half fightback by New York to clinch the best-of-five semi-final tie. Jordin Canada finished with 19 points and 11 assists for the Dream, who reached the championship series for the fourth time in franchise history and will be seeking their first title.

Atlanta completed the sweep despite playing without Allisha Gray, one of their leading scorers, who missed her second consecutive game with a left hand injury. DeWanna Bonner contributed 13 points and 13 rebounds, while Australian reserve Isobel Borlase added 10 points on five-of-six shooting.

The Dream got off to a flying start, connecting on five of their eight three-point attempts in the opening quarter. Howard scored 11 points and Reese added 10, including a pair of threes, as Atlanta established a 25-18 lead. Reese had 18 points by half-time, helping the visitors take a 44-39 advantage into the break.

highlights.title: A Cray-1 supercomputer replica from 30 "obsolete" Mac Minis
highlights.summary: The Museo de Historia de la Computación in Spain has unveiled a 1:1 scale visual replica of the famous Cray-1 supercomputer from 1976. Instead of sourcing expensive, cutting-edge tech to run the system, the creative team powered the project with 30 2012-era Mac Minis.
body: Mac Minis from over a decade ago might not seem like the obvious first choice for building a cluster supercomputer, but when networked together, the developers can orchestrate the 64 active processing cores into a combined 1.3 teraflops of performance in their most recent tests. The museum reportedly achieved 1.5 teraflops previously using all 70 available cores, prior to one node going offline. Benchmarks were obtained using a custom matrix-multiplication Python script. Five PCs are quad-core i7s, and the remaining 25 are dual-core i5 models. Except for two units from 2014, the rest of the array dates to 2012.

The replica is a valuable tool for museum-goers to understand the shifts in computer architecture since 1976. The original Cray-1 used vector processing, applying a single instruction to multiple data elements simultaneously, whereas the replica distributes work across independent processors in a parallel cluster. The peak theoretical performance of the original Cray-1 was approximately 160 megaflops. What was originally a purpose-built research machine has been re-created with consumer hardware that's vastly more capable than the machine that inspired it.

Here’s the biggest difference between Darkhold Destiny and previous Universes Beyond sets: Magic publisher Wizards of the Coast is using this one to tell an original story set within the Marvel sandbox. highlights.title: Carnegie Hall’s Opening Night Gala Spotlighted the Power of Music
highlights.summary: When the first orange-tinged leaves appear in Central Park, New Yorkers knows the Carnegie Hall fall season is just around the corner, too. On Thursday evening, the historic venue opened its doors to mark the start of its autumn program with a performance by the Berliner Philharmoniker.
body: Led by chief conductor Kirill Petrenko and featuring star tenor Jonas Kaufmann, the night’s show under the Hall’s gilded ceilings and boxes was an international display of talent. In the heart of midtown Manhattan, the German orchestra performed a program of Italian music spanning Verdi, Leoncavallo, and Respighi, among others. A raucous standing ovation—and surprise brass musicians emerging from the wings—proved no translator was needed to manage the combination of different cultures at play, as they were all united by the rousing emotion of the opera.

“It was beautiful,” Constance Wu, a longtime classical music enthusiast, told Vogue. “It was a very pastoral, woodland-type of program, which is a wonderful thing to listen to as summer turns to fall. It was a cool, dusky vibe, and the sound was incredible.”

After the performance, the celebrations continued at Cipriani 42nd Street for the event’s annual gala. With a celestial ‘Where the Stars Align’ theme, guests including designer Prabal Gurung, Peter Sarsgaard, Doris Wong, Jessica Joffe, Lena Hall, and Eletra Wiedemann were surrounded by vibrant sunflowers and flickering candlelight under the venue’s soaring columns.

highlights.title: Decade-old RAM is making a comeback
highlights.summary: CPU makers have noticed that the seemingly unending RAM price hikes are making it tough for a lot of us to upgrade our PCs. Their solution? A return to last-gen DDR4 RAM. Intel and AMD are making new CPUs that'll support the older, more affordable type of memory.
body: The RAM shortage is bringing back DDR4, with new Intel and AMD CPUs for older RAM, sockets, and chipsets.

On Friday, Gigabyte announced that two of its motherboard lines will support “upcoming” processors built on Intel’s LGA 1700 socket. That socket debuted in 2021 with the 12th gen Alder Lake CPUs and supported both DDR4 RAM and the then-new DDR5 RAM. Intel dropped it for a DDR5-only approach in 2024. But according to Gigabyte, the dual format support is now being revived, with new LGA 1700 chips “expected to launch in early 2027.”

This backtrack stems from LGA 1700’s cross-compatibility with both kinds of RAM — an advantage over its successor that’s recently become much more important. Intel’s strategy may be to offer users the choice of a new CPU that doesn’t require them to switch to new, and very expensive, DDR5 memory, too. AMD is doing something similar: in August, Gigabyte also announced a new series of motherboards for AMD’s last-gen, DDR4-compatible AM4 platform to go along with the 10th-anniversary relaunch of the Ryzen 7 5800X3D CPU.
points: CPU makers have noticed that the seemingly unending RAM price hikes are making it tough for a lot of us to upgrade our PCs.

body: Dana White has credited Eddie Hearn for making sure the long-awaited fight between Tyson Fury and Antony Joshua will be held in the UK but insisted he was "bored" of their ongoing feud.

The heavyweight bout will take place at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff - despite efforts to host it New York's Madison Square Garden - on a bill that starts on 11 December, though they are not expected to fight until the early hours of 12 December.
White and Saudi Arabian organisers wanted the bout in the United States, but Joshua and his promoter Hearn refused to budge on their contractual right to have it in the UK.

"You've got to give credit to Eddie for really grinding that and making sure that it happened in the UK," UFC president and Zuffa Boxing chief White told Steve Bunce on the 5 Live Boxing with Bunce podcast.

highlights.title: I got tired of eye-stinging campfire smoke, so I tested smokeless fire pits to find the best
highlights.summary: We put half a dozen backyard smokeless fire pits – from Solo Stove, Breeo, BioLite and more – to the test. A campfire in your backyard seems like a nice idea – until you try one and end up shifting chairs every 30 seconds to escape the eye-searing smoke.
body: New models by Cuisinart, Breeo, Solo Stove and others help you meet all of those objectives with one product.

The reduced smoke comes from the clever double-wall construction. Air intake holes at the base draw cool air between the walls, which becomes superheated and spews out holes on the top, helping to burn uncombusted particulates and reducing visible smoke. The result is a fire that burns hotter and smokes less.

For our initial backyard smokeless fire pit testing at the Filter US (a part of the Guardian US newsroom), I reviewed six models, setting them all up in my driveway at the same time. I cooked burgers and steaks, checked the smoke levels and heat and tested how long each one lasted. After a month of testing, one clear winner stood out among several other smokeless options.
As I raced around my driveway, keeping all of my little fires burning like a wildman, cooking steaks and measuring the temp and smoke levels, one fire pit stood out in the crowd.
